_comment: Registry of import sample files. Every .csv in this directory must have an
entry here, and every entry must have a file — samples_test.go fails on
either mismatch, so a sample cannot be dropped in without declaring what it
provenance is the load-bearing field. 'generated' samples were produced by
this repository's own export code and are authoritative. 'synthetic' samples
were written by hand from a vendor's documented column list and prove only
that the template matches what we believe the format to be — they cannot
confirm the belief. Replacing a synthetic sample with a 'real' one (an
actual, anonymised export from the application) is what turns a best-effort

expectRowErrorFields marks a sample whose first row legitimately cannot become a flight — the source recorded something FlightCreate requires and the file does not carry. It is not a known-failure escape hatch: the listed fields are asserted exactly, so the day the importer stops rejecting that row, or starts rejecting it for a different reason, the test fails.

expectParseError marks a sample that must be REJECTED, with the message the pilot should see. An export of an empty logbook is a real thing people upload, and telling them the file is malformed sends them hunting for a problem that is not there.
See README.md for how to contribute a real export.

samples.notes: Frozen output of writeStandardCSV. Also guards backwards compatibility: exports a pilot downloaded from an older version must keep importing.
Frozen output of writeEASACSV — the AMC1 FCL.050 column layout, H:MM durations, DD.MM.YYYY dates.
Frozen output of writeFAACSV — decimal-hour durations, MM/DD/YYYY dates, no block times.
Written from ForeFlight's documented export layout, including the Aircraft Table preamble and a structured Approach1 cell. Semicolon-delimited, as ForeFlight writes.

Real FLYLOG.io export, crew name anonymised (the same replacement in NAME_PIC and NAME_INSTRUCTOR, since one person in both cells is what the sample proves). UPPER_SNAKE_CASE headers, H:MM durations, comma-delimited. NAME_STUDENT=SELF is FLYLOG's marker for the logbook owner and must not become a contact.

Real MyFlightbook export. Fully quoted, UTF-8 BOM, 54 columns. Carries both 'Model' (marketing description: 'C-172 S, Cessna Skyhawk SP') and 'ICAO Model' (the type code) — the type must come from the latter. 'Aircraft ID' is MyFlightbook's internal numeric row ID, not a registration. Its one flight has an empty Route, which is why it cannot import.

Real LogTen Pro Dynamic Export: TAB-delimited .txt, trailing empty column, trailing blank rows. Uses the FAA short column names ('Dual Rcvd', 'Sim Inst', 'Day Ldg', 'XC'), so it was detected as FAA_CSV and imported as nothing until LOGTEN_CSV got a signature on the columns LogTen alone writes. Out/In are bare four-digit clock times ('1003'). Crew name anonymised.

Real Wader export. camelCase headers. Nothing needed anonymising: the only crew cell is the literal SELF marker. Unrecorded times are written as 00:00 rather than left blank (takeoffTime and parkingTime here), which the importer drops before deriving a block time. aircraftType is empty, so the type falls back to the registration. totalTime is empty and no on-block was recorded, so this flight imports with a zero total — incomplete source data, not a mapping fault.

Real SkyDemon export header, but of an EMPTY logbook — one header row, no flights. The column names are therefore verified and the value formats are not: it is unknown whether the time columns carry a full timestamp or a bare clock time, which decides whether a SkyDemon logbook can be dated at all (it has no date column). A populated export is still wanted. Detection is asserted on the header row; the file itself must be rejected with a message that says it has no flights.

wanted.why: We assume the long-form EASA spellings ('Departure Place', 'Name(s) PIC'). If capzlog uses the short forms it will be detected as generic EASA instead.
German club export. Column names likely vary by club configuration, so two exports from different clubs are worth more than one.
Assumed to use the mcc_/flight_ prefixed database column names. Unverified.
wanted.howToExport: mccPILOTLOG / CrewLounge PILOTLOG → File → Export → CSV.

wanted.why: SkyDemon logs sectors rather than logbook rows; we need to see which columns actually exist before promising anything.
